LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 13.1.1 EXTENSIVE LISTENING OR OBSERVING SIGNED : SPEECHES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.1: Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 13.1.1 Extensive Listening or Observing signed : Speeches
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 13.1.1 Extensive Listening or Observing signed : Speeches, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you ensure that you remember what you hear or observe from a speech?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of vocabulary related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 13.1.1 Extensive Listening or Observing signed : Speeches in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify the issue addressed by the different speeches listened to [Hard of Hearing],

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 13.1.1 Extensive Listening or Observing signed : Speeches in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. identify the issue addressed by the different signed speeches observed [Deaf],

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 13.1.1 Extensive Listening or Observing signed : Speeches in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. take notes on the points made by the different speakers on the issue,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 13.1.1 Extensive Listening or Observing signed : Speeches in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. acknowledge the importance of getting information from varied sources. • In groups, learners are guided to watch a signed demonstration or video of vocabulary related to sea travel. • In pairs, learners are guided to fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to sea travel. • Learner who is Hard of hearing is guided to search online and offline for varied speeches on an issue of interest and listen to them for enjoyment and general information. • In groups, learner who is Deaf is guided to search online and offline for varied signed speeches on an issue of interest and observe them for enjoyment and general information. • In groups, learner who is Hard of Hearing is guided to listen to or observe selected speeches on a 1. How can you ensure that you remember what you hear or observe from a speech? 2. How can you identify the issue addressed by a speech observed or listened to? 159 specific issue such as sea travel played out or read out and identify the issue addressed by the different speeches. • In groups, learner who is Deaf is guided to observe selected speeches on a specific issue such as sea travel signed out and identify the issue addressed by the different speeches. • Individually, learner is guided to in plenary, share the common theme identified to gain consensus. • In pairs, learners are guided to observe or listen to the speeches again and, take notes on the points from each of the speeches. • In groups, learners are guided to compare the notes taken by different pairs and compile the recurrent points. • Individually, learner is guided to use the points noted from the speeches to write and make a speech on the same theme. 160 • Individually, learner is guided to record and share their signed speeches on the class vlog or other social media. • In groups, learners are guided to discuss the benefits of listening to different speeches on the same subject.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 13.1.1 Extensive Listening or Observing signed : Speeches together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: global awareness skills are developed when the learner listens to and makes a speech on sea travel.

● Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with technology as the learner searches for speeches online.

Values:
Respect: the learners respectfully assess each other’s points as they compile them.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relate listening skills taught in English to similar concept of listening in Creative Arts and Sports.

Suggested Learning Resources

Word cards, Chart, Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g. tablets and mobile phones,
